full_text_en:
Shenzhen Biaobang Investment Development Co., Ltd. v. Anshan Municipal Finance Bureau — Dispute over Equity Transfer Agreement

【Ruling Summary】

1. Where the effective condition of a contract is stipulated as approval and permission, the party obligated to apply for approval shall bear liability for contracting negligence if it fails to fulfill such obligation.

2. Where the party at fault in contracting negligence gains benefits at the expense of the other party in good faith losing opportunities for transactions, the people's court shall support the claim of the party in good faith for compensation from the party at fault.

3. In addition to direct losses, the party at fault in contracting negligence shall compensate the other party in good faith for indirect losses such as loss of transaction opportunities. The amount of indirect losses shall be determined through comprehensive consideration of factors such as the degree of fault of the party at fault and the benefits obtained thereby, as well as the cost expenditures and expected benefits of the party in good faith.

Civil Judgment of the Supreme People's Court

(2016) Supreme People's Court Final Civil Case No. 802

Appellant (Plaintiff at First Instance): Shenzhen Biaobang Investment Development Co., Ltd. Domicile: Room 1316, Chuangzhan Center, South side of Chegongmiao, Shennan Avenue, Futian District, Shenzhen City, Guangdong Province.

Legal Representative: Yang Ruiqiong, Chairperson of the Board.

Agent ad litem: Chen Hao, Attorney from Beijing Yingke (Shenyang) Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Li Zongsheng, Attorney from Liaoning Anxing Law Firm.

Appellant (Defendant at First Instance): Anshan Municipal Finance Bureau. Domicile: No. 8, Shenglu South Road, Tiedong District, Anshan City, Liaoning Province.

Legal Representative: Zhang Xiaoqiang, Director of the Bureau.

Agent ad litem: Li Ying, Attorney from Liaoning Tianbo Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Wu Dongyang, Attorney from Liaoning Tianbo Law Firm.

In the case of dispute over an equity transfer agreement between the appellant, Shenzhen Biaobang Investment Development Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Biaobang Company), and the appellant, Anshan Municipal Finance Bureau (hereinafter referred to as the Anshan Finance Bureau), Biaobang Company appealed against the Civil Judgment (2015) Liaoning Second Civil First Instance No. 00060 rendered by the Liaoning High People's Court. This Court, after filing the case on December 7, 2016, formed a collegial panel in accordance with the law composed of presiding judge Zhang Nengbao as the chief judge, and judges Su Ge and Dong Hua, with the judge assistant changed from Liu Yaoguo to Sun Lei to assist in handling the case, and Liu Meiyue serving as the court clerk. A public hearing was conducted on January 10, 2017. Chen Hao and Li Zongsheng, the agents ad litem of Biaobang Company, and Li Ying, the agent ad litem of the Anshan Finance Bureau, appeared in court to participate in the proceedings. This case is now concluded.

Biaobang Company appealed with the following requests: To set aside Item 4 of the first-instance judgment and to amend the judgment to support Biaobang Company's claim for loss of expected benefits in the amount of RMB 112,500,000.00. Facts and reasons: (1) The first-instance judgment erred in finding that the Share Transfer Contract involved in the case was established but not yet effective. The notice of the State Council entitled "Notice on Strengthening the Management of State-owned Enterprise Property Rights Transactions" is a normative document of the State Council. The subject of approval under this notice is not the transaction contract, but the transfer of state-owned enterprise property rights, which has no effect on the validity of the contract. The contractual clause providing for "entry into force upon approval by the competent authority" is an invalid clause. Approval of the contract by an administrative authority does not fall within the "condition" as stipulated in Article 45 of the Contract Law. Where the parties agree that approval by an administrative authority constitutes a condition for the contract's entry into force, such agreement shall be deemed as not having been made. The auction transfer of the equity involved in this case had already been approved by the government, and the Share Transfer Contract should have been an effective contract. (2) The first-instance judgment erred in finding that the contract was rescinded through negotiation between the parties. The Anshan Finance Bureau unilaterally issued a notice to terminate the transaction and did not engage in negotiations with Biaobang Company or other enterprises. Therefore, the time of rescission should be determined as June 14, 2013, the date on which Biaobang Company received the unilateral rescission notice from the Anshan Finance Bureau. (3) The first-instance judgment erred in denying Biaobang Company's claim for loss of expected benefits. The contract had already taken effect; the Anshan Finance Bureau's unilateral rescission constituted a fundamental breach of contract and should compensate for both actual losses and loss of expected benefits. Clause 13.1 of Article 13 of the contract also explicitly stipulates that the breaching party shall compensate for all economic losses. Although the parties agreed that the equity could not be transferred within five years of acquisition, and that any transfer thereafter would require regulatory approval, the Anshan Finance Bureau's breach completely deprived Biaobang Company of the possibility of obtaining such benefits. Even if the price of Anshan Bank shares five years later is difficult to predict, the amount of compensation from the Anshan Finance Bureau can still be determined by reference to the profit gained by the Anshan Finance Bureau from the resale.

The Anshan Finance Bureau argued in defense: (1) The share transfer contract was not approved by the competent authority and is thus an unenforceable contract; the first-instance judgment's finding on this point was correct. (2) The Anshan Finance Bureau's exercise of the right to rescind the contract did not violate legal provisions and should not give rise to liability for compensation. As a real estate enterprise, Biaobang Company did not meet the conditions for equity acquisition; the source of its funds for the equity acquisition may not have been its own funds, as it was receivables. Due to Biaobang Company's own defects, the contract could not be performed and the purpose of the contract could not be realized, forcing the Anshan Finance Bureau to rescind the contract unilaterally. The share transfer contract has been rescinded, and the related issues between the parties have been resolved; Biaobang Company's lawsuit should not be supported. (3) The Anshan Finance Bureau should not compensate Biaobang Company for loss of expected benefits. The share transfer contract was not effective; the Anshan Finance Bureau's profit from the transfer is a legal gain and did not harm Biaobang Company's interests. Even if Biaobang Company had actually obtained the equity, due to the restriction on transfer periods stipulated in the contract, any subsequent transfer would require regulatory approval; therefore, Biaobang Company's claim for calculating its loss of expected benefits based on the price difference from the Anshan Finance Bureau's transfer of equity lacks legal and contractual basis. (4) The Anshan Finance Bureau should not compensate Biaobang Company for transaction fees, deposits, and corresponding interest losses. Biaobang Company had already sent a letter to Shenyang United Property Rights Exchange (ShenJiaoSuo) stating that transaction fees would not be refunded; the Anshan Finance Bureau is not at fault and had already returned the transaction fees and interest on March 17, 2014, so no further compensation should be made. It is an industry practice that no interest is paid on deposits for property rights transactions that do not result in a transaction; the Anshan Finance Bureau had already returned the deposit on October 16, 2013, and should not be liable for interest. Even if interest were to be paid on the transaction fees and deposit, it should be calculated at the benchmark deposit interest rate of the People's Bank of China for the corresponding period.

The Anshan Finance Bureau appealed with the following requests: To set aside Items 1, 2, and 3 of the first-instance judgment and to amend the judgment to hold that the Anshan Finance Bureau is not liable for compensation. Facts and reasons: (1) The Share Transfer Contract was unilaterally rescinded by notice on April 11, 2013. After the Anshan State-owned Assets Supervision and Administration Commission (Anshan SASAC) sent a letter to terminate the contract, Hongyun Group, on behalf of Biaobang Company and three other companies, sent a reply to Anshan SASAC regarding the termination. Anshan SASAC should be deemed as one of the parties to the transaction contract, and its expression of intent could be deemed as that of the Anshan Finance Bureau. After Biaobang Company received the notice of termination from Anshan SASAC, it did not file a lawsuit within three months in accordance with Article 24 of the Judicial Interpretation (II) of the Contract Law. In accordance with Article 96 of the Contract Law, the Share Transfer Notice was rescinded on April 11, 2013. On October 11, 2013, Biaobang Company, through Hongyun Group, sent a letter to the Anshan Finance Bureau requesting the return of the transaction deposit; this act constituted confirmation of the post-rescission handling of the contract that had already been rescinded by the Anshan Finance Bureau, not an agreement between the parties on the rescission. (2) The first-instance judgment erred in finding that the statute of limitations had not been exceeded. From the date of rescission on April 11, 2013, to May 26, 2015, when the Anshan Finance Bureau received Biaobang Company's "Letter Requesting Loss Compensation," Biaobang Company had never demanded compensation for losses from the Anshan Finance Bureau, nor had it stated any amount of compensation. There were no events during this period that could interrupt the statute of limitations; thus, Biaobang Company's lawsuit exceeded the statute of limitations. (3) The Anshan Finance Bureau should not bear liability for compensation. The "Notice of Acceptance of Intent to Receive" issued by ShenJiaoSuo does not prove that Biaobang Company had the qualification to acquire the equity; this notice was only a preliminary review and merely confirmed that Biaobang Company met the qualifications as an intended transferee. Upon review by Anshan SASAC, the Anshan Finance Bureau, and the Anshan Banking Regulatory Bureau, Biaobang Company's submitted materials were incomplete and failed to demonstrate that the funds were its own; its main business was real estate, which did not meet the conditions for equity acquisition. Although Anshan SASAC and the Anshan Finance Bureau terminated the contract earlier than the date the audit report was issued, based solely on Biaobang Company's business registration information and the materials it submitted, it could be determined that Biaobang Company did not meet the acquisition qualifications, without the need for the audit report. Therefore, it cannot be concluded that the Anshan Finance Bureau violated the principle of good faith. Biaobang Company did not meet the qualifications to acquire Anshan Bank's equity, and there was no need for Anshan Bank to submit the matter to the relevant government departments for review. Furthermore, the Anshan Finance Bureau was not responsible for submitting for approval; that obligation rested with Anshan Bank.

Biaobang Company argued in defense: (1) The first-instance judgment erred in finding that the contract was rescinded by agreement; the contract in this case was unilaterally rescinded by the Anshan Bank's breach. The Anshan Finance Bureau entered into the share transfer contract after receiving approval from the Anshan Municipal Government. According to relevant regulations, the transfer of state-owned equity in the financial and tobacco systems is managed by the finance bureau and does not require approval from the SASAC. The contract had already been approved by the Anshan Banking Regulatory Bureau and was effective. The Anshan Finance Bureau's rescission on the ground of an affiliated relationship was unfounded, and there was no evidence of any breach by Biaobang Company. In fact, the Anshan Finance Bureau rescinded the contract because the equity price had risen, which constituted a breach of contract. (2) The first-instance judgment correctly ordered the Anshan Finance Bureau to pay the deposit, transaction fees, and interest. Biaobang Company's request for the return of the deposit was not an acknowledgment of the Anshan Finance Bureau's rescission but a measure to mitigate its losses, and it did not waive its right to claim compensation for losses.

Biaobang Company filed a lawsuit in the first-instance court with the following requests: 1. To order the Anshan Finance Bureau to compensate Biaobang Company for transaction costs in the amount of RMB 278,465.35 and interest losses on such costs up to the date of payment in the amount of RMB 56,016.79 (temporarily calculated as of the date of filing the complaint); 2. To order the Anshan Finance Bureau to compensate Biaobang Company for interest losses on the transaction deposit in the amount of RMB 1,575,539.51; 3. To order the Anshan Finance Bureau to compensate Biaobang Company for loss of expected benefits from the transaction in the amount of RMB 112,500,000; 4. To order the Anshan Finance Bureau to pay Biaobang Company's litigation-related expenses incurred in protecting its rights, including the case acceptance fee.

The first-instance court found the following facts: On November 29, 2011, the Anshan Finance Bureau, as the principal, and ShenJiaoSuo, as the agent, entered into a "Property Rights Transfer Listing Registration Agency Agreement," stipulating that the Anshan Finance Bureau, as the transferor, would entrust the registration and listing of the information regarding the transfer of the subject asset, namely 693 million shares of state-owned equity in Anshan Bank, with the Shenyang United Property Rights Exchange.

On December 30, 2011, a listing announcement was published on the ShenJiaoSuo website for the transfer by the Anshan Finance Bureau of 27.7161% equity (693 million shares), including details of the share transfer, transfer price, conditions for eligibility of transferee shareholders, proportion and amount of the deposit, and listing period. At the same time, the "Anshan Bank State-owned Equity Transfer Investment Prospectus" was published on the ShenJiaoSuo website's investment information page. The prospectus stated that the project for the transfer of 32.3155% state-owned equity of Anshan Bank was published as a listing announcement on the Liaoning Daily and the ShenJiaoSuo website on December 30, 2011. To enable investors to understand Anshan Bank, the prospectus provided information on the overview of Anshan City, the basic situation of Anshan Bank, future development directions, and the state-owned equity structure.

On February 24, 2012, on behalf of four delisting enterprises, Hongyun Group paid RMB 35 million as a deposit for the equity transfer to the Anshan Finance Bureau. On the same day, it paid an additional RMB 13.48 million (calculated as 3% of the total listing price of 808 million shares, which was RMB 1.616 billion, totaling RMB 48.48 million, including RMB 13.5 million to be paid by Biaobang Company in this case).

On March 21, 2012, Biaobang Company submitted the delisting materials required in the listing announcement to ShenJiaoSuo.

On March 28, 2012, four companies—Liaoning Rongxin Asset Management Co., Ltd., CITIC Honghe Mining Co., Ltd., Biaobang Company, and Hongyun Group Co., Ltd.—succeeded in the delisting process. Biaobang Company obtained 275 million shares, including the 225 million shares of the Anshan Finance Bureau involved in this case, as well as 50 million shares from Haicheng Magnesite Refractory Material General Plant.

On March 29, 2012, ShenJiaoSuo issued to Biaobang Company the "Notice of Acceptance of Intent to Receive" under numbers GQ2011018, GQ2011019, and GQ2011021. The notice stated: Biaobang Company: We have received the delisting materials you submitted to ShenJiaoSuo on March 21, 2012, for the project involving the transfer of 275 million shares of Anshan Bank. After joint review with the transferor, we believe that your company meets the qualifications as an intended transferee and hereby accept your application. Please deposit the delisting deposit of RMB 16.5 million (RMB 13.5 million in this case) into our account before 5:00 p.m. on March 30, 2012. If the deposit is not paid within the specified time, you will be deemed to have voluntarily waived your qualification to acquire.

On March 30, 2012, Biaobang Company paid a deposit of RMB 16.5 million (RMB 13.5 million in this case) to ShenJiaoSuo.

On April 17, 2012, the transferor, the Anshan Finance Bureau (Party A), and the transferee, Biaobang Company (Party B), entered into a Share Transfer Contract numbered 2012-jr003. The main terms of the contract were as follows: Whereas Party A intends to transfer its legally held 9.9986% equity interest, i.e., 225 million shares, in the target company, and Party B intends to acquire the said shares from Party A, the parties enter into this equity transaction contract as follows: 1.5 Valuation Base Date: The base date on which the accounting firm with legal qualifications appointed by Party A conducts the valuation and issues the "Asset Appraisal Report"; 1.6 Deposit: The transaction deposit paid by Party B to the account designated by Party A and ShenJiaoSuo before the signing of this contract, in accordance with the requirements of Party A and ShenJiaoSuo, as a guarantee for Party B's intention to acquire and to demonstrate its financial standing and performance capability; 1.7 Approving Authorities: Including the China Banking Regulatory Commission, Anshan SASAC, and other authorities with approval authority under national laws, regulations, or their local authorized agencies; 1.8 Registration Authority: The State Administration for Industry and Commerce of the People's Republic of China or its local authorized agencies; 1.9 Property Transaction Costs: All cash outlays and costs incurred by the transferor and/or transferee or the target company in connection with the transfer of property rights or the negotiation, preparation, execution of this contract and/or any documents hereunder, or the performance or completion of the transactions contemplated hereunder, including costs and expenses incurred in obtaining necessary or appropriate exemptions, consents, or approvals from any government authorities or third parties, as well as the fees of the property rights transaction institution. 1.10 Property Transaction Certificate: The certificate issued by ShenJiaoSuo for the purpose of the share transfer, indicating that the on-exchange transaction procedures have been completed in accordance with the transaction rules. 2.1 The target company involved in this contract, Anshan Bank, is a limited liability company with an independent corporate legal person status legally existing. Its main business scope includes accepting deposits from the public, granting loans, handling domestic settlement, bill discounting, and issuing financial bonds. Its registered capital is RMB 2,500.35 million, with a total number of shares of 2,500.35 million; 2.2 The target company was appraised by Anshan Xincheng Asset Appraisal Firm, which possesses appraisal qualifications, and issued the "Asset Appraisal Report" (An Xin Cheng Ping Bao Zi [2011] No. 04010) with the valuation base date of December 31, 2010. After verification and filing by Anshan SASAC, the net assets of the enterprise were RMB 4,940.06 million; 2.3 The target company has no matters that are not disclosed or omitted in the "Asset Appraisal Report" that may affect the appraisal results or have a material adverse effect on the target company or the value of its shares; 2.4 Both Party A and Party B reached the terms of this contract on the basis of the appraisal results of the target company's "Asset Appraisal Report".

Article 3: Subject Matter of Equity Transfer

3.1 Party A transfers to Party B 8.9987% of the shares of the Target Company, equivalent to 225,000,000 shares (hereinafter referred to as the "Equity"), at a price of RMB 500,000,000 (RMB 2.00 per share).

3.2 Party A has fully paid up the subscribed capital contributions in respect of the Equity subject to transfer.

3.3 The Equity subject to transfer has not been subject to any form of security, including any pledge on such equity or any restriction or obligation affecting the transfer of equity or the exercise of shareholders' rights. The Equity subject to transfer has also not been subject to any compulsory measures such as seizure by any competent authority.

Article 4: Conditions Precedent for Equity Transfer

4.1 Party A has completed the public listing procedure at the Shenyang Property Rights Exchange (Shenyang Exchange) in respect of the equity transaction under this Contract in accordance with the provisions of relevant laws, regulations and policies.

4.2 Party B, in accepting the transfer of the Equity held by Party A under this Contract, has performed the approval or authorization procedures in accordance with the law and the provisions of the articles of association.

Article 5: Method of Equity Transfer

The equity transaction under this Contract was publicly listed on the Shenyang Exchange for 20 working days on December 30, 2011, and the listing was extended to March 28, 2012. During the extended listing period, only one意向 transferee, Party B, emerged for the Equity subject to transfer, and Party B accepted the transfer of the Equity under this Contract in accordance with the law.

6.1 Transfer Price: Based on the public listing results, Party A transfers the Equity subject to transfer under this Contract to Party B at a price of RMB 450,000,000 (in words: RMB Four Hundred and Fifty Million Yuan only).

6.2 Party B has paid a transaction deposit of RMB 13,500,000 as required by Party A and the Shenyang Exchange. The deposit shall be converted into part of the transaction price and paid to Party A after the Shenyang Exchange issues the transaction certificate.

6.3 After this equity transfer is approved by the approving authority, Party B shall transfer the transaction price into the settlement account of the Shenyang Exchange in accordance with relevant state regulations. The transaction price shall be paid in full in a single lump sum by currency within 7 working days.

Article 7: Approval and Registration

7.1 This transfer shall be submitted to the competent approving authority for approval in accordance with the law. Both Party A and Party B shall perform or assist in performing the obligation to submit applications to the approving authority, and shall use their best efforts to cooperate in addressing any reasonable requests and inquiries raised by the approving authority, in order to obtain the approval of the approving authority for this Contract and the equity transaction thereunder.

7.2 Within 5 working days after the equity transaction under this Contract is approved by the approving authority and the Shenyang Exchange issues the property rights transaction certificate, Party A shall propose amendments to the articles of association of the Target Company and complete the procedures for registering the change of shares of the Target Company with the registration authority. Party B shall provide necessary assistance and cooperation.

Article 8: Taxes and Fees

8.1 Party A and Party B shall bear their respective taxes payable during the transaction in accordance with relevant legal provisions.

8.2 In accordance with relevant agreements, the transaction service fees incurred during the equity transaction shall be paid by Party A and Party B respectively to the Shenyang Exchange.

Article 9: This share transfer does not involve any employee placement issues.

Article 10: Party A warrants that:

10.1 It has legal, valid and complete rights of disposal over the Equity subject to transfer under this Contract.

10.2 All certifications and materials submitted to Party B and the Shenyang Exchange for the purpose of entering into this Contract are true, accurate and complete.

10.3 All procedures required for entering into this Contract, including authorization, approval and internal corporate decisions, have been legally and validly obtained, and the conditions precedent for the formation of this Contract and the equity transfer have been satisfied.

10.4 The Equity subject to transfer is not subject to any security or restriction that may affect the equity transfer.

Article 11: Party B warrants that:

11.1 The acceptance of the Equity subject to transfer under this Contract complies with the provisions of laws and regulations and does not violate the industrial policies within the territory of China.

11.2 All certifications and materials submitted to Party A and the Shenyang Exchange for the purpose of entering into this Contract are true, accurate and complete.

11.3 All approval procedures required for entering into this Contract, including authorization, approval and internal corporate decisions, have been legally and validly obtained, and the conditions precedent for the formation of this Contract and the acceptance of the equity transfer have been satisfied.

11.4 It shall comply with national laws, administrative regulations and the articles of association of the Target Company, and perform the rights and obligations of a shareholder.

The principal shareholders of the Target Company undertake: not to seek related transactions superior to those of other shareholders; not to interfere with the daily operations of the bank; not to transfer their shares in the Target Company within 5 years from the date of share delivery, and this shall be stated in the articles of association of the Target Company; upon the expiry of such period, any transfer of shares and the shareholder qualification of the transferee shall be subject to the consent of the regulatory authorities; to continuously replenish capital and not to impose undue performance pressure on the Target Company.

Article 12: Rights and Obligations

12.1 Rights and Obligations of Party A:

(1) If, prior to the completion of the share change registration with the administrative department for industry and commerce, the Equity subject to transfer becomes subject to any pledge or any restriction or obligation affecting the equity transfer or the exercise of shareholders' rights, Party A shall bear the losses caused thereby to the relevant parties to the transaction.

(2) After this Contract becomes effective, Party A has the obligation to collect the transfer price in accordance with the contract, and to assist and cooperate with Party B in completing relevant procedures such as the certification of equity and the share change registration with the administrative department for industry and commerce.

12.2 Rights and Obligations of Party B:

(1) If, from the date of signing this Contract until the completion of the share change registration with the administrative department for industry and commerce, Party B transfers the rights and interests in the Equity subject to transfer to a third party, creates an external security, or incurs any restriction or obligation affecting the equity transfer or the exercise of shareholders' rights, Party B shall bear the losses caused thereby to the relevant parties to the transaction.

(2) After this Contract becomes effective, Party B shall perform the obligations of a shareholder in accordance with the provisions of the articles of association, share profits, and bear risks and losses.

12.3 Rights and Obligations of Both Party A and Party B:

(1) After this Contract becomes effective, Party A and Party B shall, in accordance with relevant regulations, proceed with the equity transfer transaction procedures at the Shenyang Exchange and pay relevant fees according to relevant regulations.

(2) After this Contract is approved, Party A and Party B shall cooperate with each other and promptly proceed with the relevant change registration procedures with the administrative department for industry and commerce and other authorities.

Article 13: Liability for Breach of Contract

13.1 If this Contract cannot be performed due to reasons attributable to Party A, Party A shall be deemed to be in complete breach, and shall compensate Party B for all economic losses and bear liability for breach of contract.

13.2 If the transaction price cannot be timely remitted to the account designated by the Shenyang Exchange in accordance with this Contract due to reasons attributable to Party B, Party B shall be deemed to be in complete breach; Party A has the right to request the cancellation of Party B's qualification as transferee, to rescind and terminate the performance of this Contract, and the transaction deposit shall not be refunded. Party A also has the right to initiate legal proceedings against Party B to claim compensation for corresponding economic losses.

13.3 If Party A or Party B fails to perform all or part of its obligations under this Contract and the appendices, it shall be deemed a breach, and the breaching party shall compensate the non-breaching party for all economic losses caused thereby.

Article 14: Amendment and Rescission of the Contract

14.1 If Party A and Party B need to amend all or part of the terms of this Contract, they must sign a written agreement and submit it to the original approving authority for approval, and file a copy with the Shenyang Exchange for archival purposes.

14.2 If one party's breach of contract causes serious losses to the non-breaching party, the breaching party shall be deemed to have unilaterally terminated this Contract. The non-breaching party has the right to claim liquidated damages from the breaching party (equivalent to all losses caused to the non-breaching party by the breaching party's breach) and also has the right, in accordance with the contract, to report to the original approving authority for approval to terminate this Contract.

14.3 If this Contract cannot be performed due to force majeure, the contract shall automatically terminate, and both parties shall be relieved of liability.

Article 15: Jurisdiction and Dispute Resolution

15.1 This Contract and the acts in the equity transaction shall be governed by the laws of the People's Republic of China.

15.2 Any dispute between the parties arising from the interpretation or performance of this Contract shall be resolved through negotiation. If negotiation fails, a lawsuit may be filed in a competent people's court at the place where the Target Company is located.

Article 16: Effectiveness of the Contract

This Contract shall become effective upon being signed and sealed by the legal representatives or authorized representatives of Party A and Party B, and upon being approved by the competent approving authority in accordance with laws and administrative regulations.

17.1 Any amendments or supplements to the content of this Contract, or matters not covered herein, shall be negotiated and concluded in writing by the parties and shall serve as appendices to this Contract. The appendices to this Contract shall have the same legal effect as this Contract.

17.2 The letters of undertaking and other documents submitted by Party B in accordance with the listing conditions during the acceptance of the Equity subject to transfer shall be an integral part of this Contract and shall have the same legal effect as this Contract.

17.3 This Contract is executed in 10 originals, with each of Party A and Party B holding one copy, Anshan Bank holding one copy; and one copy each for archival purposes with the China Banking Regulatory Commission, the Shenyang Exchange, and the administrative department for industry and commerce. The remaining copies shall be used for approval and registration procedures for the equity transaction. All copies shall have the same legal effect.

On February 10, 2012, Biaobang Company submitted the relevant approval materials to Anshan Bank as agreed in the contract between the parties. In the submitted materials, Biaobang Company made written commitments and declarations that it would not seek related transactions superior to those of other shareholders, would not interfere with the daily operations of the bank, would not transfer its shares within five years, and would not engage in illegal related transactions.

In June 2012, Anshan Bank submitted to the Anshan Supervision Office of the China Banking Regulatory Commission (CBRC) the "Request for Qualification Review of Biaobang Company and One Other Enterprise as Shareholders of Anshan Bank", accompanied by a list of application materials.

On June 12, 2012, the Anshan Supervision Office of the CBRC submitted to the Liaoning Banking Regulatory Bureau a document, An Yin Jian Fa [2012] No. 165, titled "Supervisory Opinion on the Change of Shareholders of Anshan Bank Co., Ltd. in 2012". The opinion stated:

"Liaoning Banking Regulatory Bureau: Recently, our bureau received the 'Request for Qualification Review of Biaobang Company and One Other Enterprise as Shareholders of Anshan Bank' submitted by Anshan Bank. Pursuant to the 'Law of the People's Republic of China on Banking Regulation and Supervision' and the relevant requirements of the 'Implementation Measures for Administrative Licensing Matters for Chinese-funded Commercial Banks' of the CBRC, our bureau conducted a preliminary review of the change of shareholders of Anshan Bank. We now report the relevant circumstances as follows: As of the date hereof, the total share capital of Anshan Bank is RMB 2,500,350,000, of which state shares and state-owned legal person shares amount to RMB 1,448,000,000, accounting for 57.91% of the total share capital; corporate legal person shares amount to RMB 972,805,500, accounting for 38.91%; and individual shares amount to RMB 79,548,500, accounting for 3.18%. The total number of shares involved in this change of shareholders of Anshan Bank is 333,000,000 shares, of which Anshan Finance Bureau transfers 243,000,000 shares, with the transferees being Biaobang Company (225,000,000 shares) and Hongyun Group Company (18,000,000 shares); Haicheng Magnesite Refractory Materials General Plant transfers 90,000,000 shares, with the transferees being Biaobang Company (50,000,000 shares) and Hongyun Group Co., Ltd. (40,000,000 shares). The transfer price is RMB 2 per share. Anshan Bank has submitted the corresponding application materials in accordance with the requirements for the approval of changes in shareholders' shareholdings in Chinese-funded commercial banks. The application materials basically meet the requirements of the CBRC's catalogue and format for administrative licensing application materials. After this change of shareholders of Anshan Bank, the proportion of state-owned shares will further decrease, and the equity structure will be further adjusted, completely changing the situation of state-owned shares being overwhelmingly dominant, which is conducive to its sustained, stable and healthy development. In summary, our bureau intends to approve the relevant administrative licensing matters for this change of shareholders of Anshan Bank."

On June 12, 2012, the Anshan State-owned Assets Supervision and Administration Commission (SASAC), Biaobang Company, Hongyun Group, CITIC Honghe Mining Co., Ltd., and Liaoning Rongxin Asset Management Co., Ltd. sent a letter to the Shenyang Exchange, making a commitment regarding the transaction fees: "Regardless of whether the transferee enterprise passes the approval of the banking regulatory authority or whether the transfer is not completed due to any reason on the part of the transferor or transferee, these fees shall be paid normally."

On July 3, 2012, Biaobang Company and three other successful bidding enterprises received from the Shenyang Exchange the refund of the deposit of RMB 46,480,000 (including RMB 12,943,069.3 in this case), after deducting RMB 2,000,000 in transaction fees.

The above matters all evidence that the company is related to the real estate industry. Apart from the above matters, the company did not provide other materials related to its industry. Due to the limited information provided by the company, we are unable to determine whether the company belongs to a non-restricted industry and whether it can acquire shares in a city commercial bank.
