The letter stated: To Anshan Finance Bureau: Our group has received the "Letter Regarding Termination of the Acquisition of State-Owned Shares of Anshan Bank" from Anshan SASAC, which proposed to terminate the transfer of 808 million shares of Anshan Bank between Hongyun Group and three other enterprises with Anshan Finance Bureau and Haicheng Magnesite Refractory Material General Plant, and informed that the refund of the deposit should be handled with Anshan Finance Bureau. The four enterprises proposed that they hoped to continue performance in accordance with the original agreement and resume the transaction, but your bureau clearly stated that this could not be achieved. In view of this, our group, on behalf of each acquiring enterprise, requests Anshan Finance Bureau to refund the deposit and pay the transaction fees. Please return RMB 49.48 million (including RMB 48.48 million deposit and RMB 1 million transaction fees) to us within three days from the date of receipt of this letter. This letter is for your information.

On October 16, 2013, Biaobang Company authorized Hongyun Group to collect the refunded deposit on its behalf. On the same day, Biaobang Company and other acquiring enterprises received RMB 48.48 million in refunded deposit from Anshan Finance Bureau (including RMB 13.5 million involved in this case).

On December 31, 2013, Anshan Finance Bureau relisted the above shares for transfer at the Beijing Financial Assets Exchange.

On January 16, 2014, Biaobang Company filed a lawsuit with the first-instance court, requesting a judgment ordering Anshan Finance Bureau to continue performing the contract and to bear all litigation costs. On July 24, 2014, Anshan Finance Bureau transferred 500 million shares of the involved equity to China Huayang Investment Co., Ltd. at a price of RMB 2.5 per share, which was RMB 0.5 higher than the contractual price. On December 23, 2014, the first-instance court issued Civil Ruling No. (2014) Liao Min Er Chu Zi No. 00004, dismissing Biaobang Company's lawsuit.

On May 20, 2015, Hongyun Group, Liaoning Rongxin Asset Management Co., Ltd., CITIC Honghe Mining Co., Ltd., and Biaobang Company sent a "Letter Regarding Request for Compensation for Losses" to Anshan Finance Bureau and Haicheng Magnesite Refractory Material General Plant, requesting compensation for transaction costs, expected benefits, interest on the delisting deposit, and other losses. Anshan Finance Bureau signed for receipt of the letter on May 26, 2015, but did not respond.

On September 1, 2015, Biaobang Company initiated this lawsuit with the first-instance court.

Additionally, it was found that: during the trial, Anshan Finance Bureau submitted a written application to the first-instance court, requesting an audit of Biaobang Company's financial status for the three consecutive years from 2009 to 2011 to confirm whether it had sufficient own funds to acquire shares in Anshan Bank.

The first-instance court held that the "Entrustment Agreement for Listing Registration of Property Rights Transfer" signed between Anshan Finance Bureau and Shenyang United Property Rights Exchange and the "Share Transfer Contract" No. 2012-jr003 signed between Anshan Finance Bureau and Biaobang Company were all true expressions of the parties' intent, the parties had legal capacity, and the contract content and transaction procedures did not violate mandatory provisions of laws or regulations, nor were there any circumstances under Article 52 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China rendering the contract void; thus they should be legally valid.

The disputed issues in this case are: (1) Whether the Share Transfer Contract No. 2012-jr003 signed between Anshan Finance Bureau and Biaobang Company was formed but not yet effective; (2) Whether the Share Transfer Contract No. 2012-jr003 signed between Anshan Finance Bureau and Biaobang Company has been rescinded; (3) Whether the statute of limitations has expired in this case; (4) Whether Anshan Finance Bureau should compensate Biaobang Company for transaction costs, deposit interest, and loss of expected profit from the transaction.

(1) Regarding the issue of whether the Share Transfer Contract No. 2012-jr003 signed between Anshan Finance Bureau and Biaobang Company was formed but not yet effective. Article 44 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China provides: "A contract lawfully formed shall become effective upon its formation. Where a contract is subject to approval or registration and other procedures under laws or administrative regulations before it becomes effective, such provisions shall be followed." Article 2 of the "Notice on Strengthening the Management of State-Owned Enterprise Property Rights Transactions" (Guo Ban Fa Dian [1994] No. 12) issued by the General Office of the State Council provides: "The transfer of property rights of state-owned enterprises managed by local governments shall be approved by the people's government at or above the prefecture level. If there is investment from the central government, the consent of the relevant department of the State Council shall be obtained in advance. The property rights income from the central investment part shall belong to the central government. The transfer of property rights of state-owned enterprises managed by the central government shall be reported by the relevant department of the State Council to the State Council for approval. The property rights transfer of all super-large and large state-owned enterprises (including those managed by local governments) shall be reported to the State Council for approval." Article 16 of the Share Transfer Contract No. 2012-jr003 signed between Anshan Finance Bureau and Biaobang Company stipulates: "This contract shall become effective upon the signature and seal of the legal representatives or authorized representatives of Party A and Party B, and after obtaining the approval of the competent authority in accordance with laws and administrative regulations." Therefore, in this case, the transfer of state-owned shares of Anshan Bank held by Anshan Finance Bureau only became effective after being approved by the government department at the corresponding level in accordance with the above provisions. The Share Transfer Contract No. 2012-jr003 in question was not approved by a government department; thus the contract was formed but not yet effective. Accordingly, the court supports Anshan Finance Bureau's claim that the contract in question was formed but not yet effective, as it has factual and legal basis.

(2) Regarding the issue of whether the Share Transfer Contract No. 2012-jr003 signed between Anshan Finance Bureau and Biaobang Company has been rescinded. Article 93(1) of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China provides: "The parties may rescind the contract if they reach a consensus through consultation." In this case, on March 25, 2013, Anshan SASAC sent a letter to Hongyun Group and three other enterprises, letter No. An Guo Zi Han [2013] No. 13, proposing to terminate the transaction on the grounds that the four enterprises including Hongyun Group had related party transactions and would not pass approval. On March 27, 2013, Anshan SASAC sent a letter to Shenyang United Property Rights Exchange, letter No. An Guo Zi Han [2013] No. 15, requesting termination of the transaction. On April 11, 2013, the four companies including Hongyun Group raised objections to "An Guo Zi Han [2013] No. 13," requesting continued performance of the contract. In response to the objections raised by the four companies including Hongyun Group, Anshan SASAC entrusted an accounting firm to audit the materials submitted by the four enterprises for reporting. Before the audit results were produced, on June 6, 2013, Anshan Finance Bureau sent a letter to Shenyang United Property Rights Exchange, letter No. An Cai Zhai [2013] No. 137, concerning the termination of the transfer of state-owned shares of Anshan Bank, citing the obvious appreciation of state-owned assets, and again proposed to terminate the transfer. On June 14, 2013, Shenyang United Property Rights Exchange, based on the termination letter from Anshan Finance Bureau, issued a notice to Biaobang Company, Hongyun Group, CITIC Honghe Mining Co., Ltd., and Liaoning Rongxin Asset Management Co., Ltd. regarding the termination of the transfer of state-owned shares of Anshan Bank. On October 11, 2013, Hongyun Group, on behalf of the four listed companies, sent a letter to Anshan Finance Bureau requesting the return of the transaction deposit. From the content of that letter: (1) Hongyun Group, on behalf of the four listed companies, had received the letter from Anshan SASAC regarding the termination of the acquisition of state-owned shares of Anshan Bank; (2) Anshan SASAC proposed to terminate the share transfer and informed them about the refund of the deposit and related procedures; (3) Hongyun Group, on behalf of the four listed companies, stated: "In view of this, our group, on behalf of each acquiring enterprise, requests Anshan Finance Bureau to refund the deposit and pay the transaction fees." From the above process, including Anshan SASAC proposing to terminate the contract, Hongyun Group on behalf of the four listed companies raising objections, to Anshan SASAC again proposing to terminate the contract and refund the deposit, and Hongyun Group on behalf of the four listed companies requesting the refund of the deposit and payment of transaction fees, it can be proven that Hongyun Group, on behalf of the four listed companies, agreed to rescind the contract. Accordingly, it can be determined that the Share Transfer Contract No. 2012-jr003 signed between the parties was rescinded by agreement on October 11, 2013. Therefore, the court supports Anshan Finance Bureau's claim that the Share Transfer Contract has been rescinded.

(3) Regarding the issue of whether the statute of limitations has expired in this case. The contract in question was rescinded by agreement on October 11, 2013. On May 20, 2015, Biaobang Company submitted a claim for compensation for losses to Anshan Finance Bureau. On September 1, 2015, it initiated this lawsuit. The statute of limitations has not expired in this case. Accordingly, the court does not support Anshan Finance Bureau's defense that the statute of limitations has expired, as it lacks factual basis.

(4) Regarding the issue of whether Anshan Finance Bureau should compensate Biaobang Company for transaction costs, deposit interest, and loss of expected profit from the transaction. After the Share Transfer Contract in question was signed, Biaobang Company, based on its reliance on Anshan Finance Bureau, performed its contractual obligations including payment of the deposit and submission of application materials as stipulated in the contract. Anshan Finance Bureau should, as agreed in the contract, review Biaobang Company's qualifications for acquiring the shares based on the materials submitted by Biaobang Company, handle the approval procedures, and facilitate the contract's effectiveness. However, during performance of the contract, before the audit results were produced, without approval from a government department, and without evidence proving that Biaobang Company did not meet the acquisition conditions, Anshan SASAC and Anshan Finance Bureau, on March 25, 2013, March 27, 2013, and June 6, 2013, respectively, sent letters to the four listed companies including Hongyun Group and Shenyang United Property Rights Exchange to terminate the acquisition of state-owned shares of Anshan Bank, citing related party transactions among the four enterprises including Hongyun Group, appreciation of state-owned assets, and that approval would not be obtained. This resulted in the Share Transfer Contract being formed but not effective and subsequently rescinded. Later, Anshan Finance Bureau transferred the shares to another party. This conduct is contrary to the principle of good faith. According to Article 42 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China, which provides that "Where a party, in the course of concluding a contract, has other conduct that violates the principle of good faith, causing loss to the other party, it shall bear liability for damages," and Article 8 of the Supreme People's Court's Interpretation (II) of Several Issues Concerning the Application of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China, which provides that "Where, after the formation of a contract that requires approval or registration to become effective in accordance with laws or administrative regulations, a party obligated to apply for approval or registration fails to do so in accordance with legal provisions or contractual stipulations, such conduct constitutes 'other conduct that violates the principle of good faith' under Article 42(3) of the Contract Law. The people's court may, based on the specific circumstances of the case and the request of the counterparty, order the counterparty to handle the relevant procedures itself. The other party shall bear liability for damages for the resulting expenses and actual losses caused to the counterparty." Article 97 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China provides: "After a contract is rescinded, for obligations not yet performed, performance shall be terminated; for obligations already performed, the party may, based on the nature of the performance and the nature of the contract, demand restoration to the original state, take other remedial measures, and claim damages." Accordingly, after the Share Transfer Contract in question was formed but not effective and then rescinded, Biaobang Company is entitled to claim damages from Anshan Finance Bureau.

Regarding Biaobang Company's claim for loss of transaction costs and corresponding interest loss. According to the facts found, after the four acquiring enterprises including Biaobang Company were delisted, they paid transaction costs of RMB 1 million (including RMB 278,465.35 involved in this case) that the acquirers should pay to Shenyang United Property Rights Exchange on March 30, 2012. This amount has not been refunded to date, causing actual loss to Biaobang Company. Anshan Finance Bureau should refund the principal of the transaction costs of RMB 278,465.35 and pay interest loss at the bank loan benchmark interest rate for the corresponding period from March 30, 2012, to the date of actual payment. Therefore, the court supports Biaobang Company's claim that Anshan Finance Bureau should bear the loss of transaction costs and corresponding interest loss.

Regarding Biaobang Company's claim for loss of interest on the transaction deposit. After the four acquiring enterprises including Biaobang Company were delisted, they paid the transaction deposit twice. First, a deposit of RMB 13.5 million was paid to Anshan Finance Bureau on February 24, 2012, and was refunded by Anshan Finance Bureau on October 16, 2013. Second, a deposit of RMB 12,943,069.3 was paid to Shenyang United Property Rights Exchange on March 30, 2012, and was refunded on July 2, 2012. Anshan Finance Bureau should compensate for interest loss at the bank loan benchmark interest rate for the corresponding period from March 30, 2012, to the date of actual payment. The court supports Biaobang Company's claim that Anshan Finance Bureau should compensate for the interest loss on the deposit.

Regarding Biaobang Company's claim for loss of expected profit. Biaobang Company argues that the parties agreed that Anshan Finance Bureau would transfer 225 million shares of its shares in Anshan Bank to Biaobang Company at a price of RMB 2 per share. During performance of the contract, Anshan Finance Bureau transferred the shares to another party at RMB 2.50 per share, causing the contract to be unperformable. Anshan Finance Bureau should compensate for the loss of expected profit of (2.50 - 2.00) yuan x 225 million shares = RMB 112.5 million. Because the Share Transfer Contract No. 2012-jr003 was formed but not effective. Article 113(1) of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China provides: "If a party fails to perform its contractual obligations or performs them in a manner that does not conform to the agreement, causing loss to the other party, the amount of damages shall be equal to the loss caused by the breach, including the benefits obtainable after performance of the contract, but shall not exceed the loss that the party in breach foresaw or should have foreseen at the time of entering into the contract as a possible consequence of the breach." According to Article 42 of the Contract Law and Article 8 of the Supreme People's Court's Interpretation (II) of Several Issues Concerning the Application of the Contract Law, Anshan Finance Bureau should bear liability for damages in the nature of pre-contractual fault, compensating only the actual losses caused to Biaobang Company. Accordingly, expected profit refers to the net profit obtainable after performance of the contract, excluding the expenses incurred to obtain such profits. In this case, Article 11.4 of the Share Transfer Contract No. 2012-jr003 stipulates that Party B, Biaobang Company, declares and guarantees that it will not transfer its shares in the target enterprise within five years from the date of share delivery, and any transfer upon expiry shall be subject to regulatory approval. The listing documents also clearly stated that the acquiring enterprise would not transfer the purchased shares within five years. Given the above stipulations, even if Biaobang Company had obtained approval from the competent authority to become a shareholder of Anshan Bank, it could not transfer the shares within five years of acquisition. The share price and net profit loss from trading after five years cannot be determined. Therefore, Biaobang Company cannot use the difference of RMB 0.5 per share between the listing price of RMB 2.5 per share on December 31, 2013, and the contractual price of RMB 2 per share as the basis for claiming loss of expected profit from the transaction. Accordingly, the court does not support Biaobang Company's claim that Anshan Finance Bureau should compensate for loss of expected profit from the transaction.

Regarding Anshan Finance Bureau's application to conduct a financial audit of Biaobang Company. The burden of proving that Biaobang Company qualifies as the subject to acquire the shares lies with Anshan Finance Bureau, not with Biaobang Company. Now Anshan Finance Bureau cannot provide evidence to support its claim and applies to the court to audit Biaobang Company's financial accounts. This is without legal basis. Therefore, this application is not supported. Additionally, Anshan Finance Bureau's defense that Biaobang Company breached the contract and lacked the qualifications to acquire the shares, and that it should not bear liability for damages, is without factual and legal basis and is not supported.

In summary, Biaobang Company's claims that Anshan Finance Bureau should compensate for transaction costs loss and corresponding interest on transaction costs and deposits have factual and legal basis and are supported. Pursuant to Articles 42, 44, 93(1), 97, and 113(1) of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China, and Article 8 of the Supreme People's Court's Interpretation (II) of Several Issues Concerning the Application of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China, the judgment is as follows: 1. Anshan Finance Bureau shall, within ten days from the date this judgment takes legal effect, compensate Shenzhen Biaobang Investment Development Co., Ltd. for the principal amount of transaction costs of RMB 278,465.35 and corresponding interest (calculated from March 30, 2012, to the date of actual payment, at the bank loan benchmark interest rate for the corresponding period); 2. Anshan Finance Bureau shall, within ten days from the date this judgment takes legal effect, compensate Shenzhen Biaobang Investment Development Co., Ltd. for interest loss on the deposit of RMB 13.5 million (based on RMB 13.5 million, calculated from February 24, 2012, to October 16, 2013, at the bank loan benchmark interest rate for the corresponding period); 3. Anshan Finance Bureau shall, within ten days from the date this judgment takes legal effect, compensate Shenzhen Biaobang Investment Development Co., Ltd. for interest loss on the deposit of RMB 12,943,069.3 (based on RMB 12,943,069.3, calculated from March 30, 2012, to July 2, 2012, at the bank loan benchmark interest rate for the corresponding period); 4. All other claims of Shenzhen Biaobang Investment Development Co., Ltd. are dismissed. Court acceptance fee of RMB 613,850 shall be borne by Shenzhen Biaobang Investment Development Co., Ltd. in the amount of RMB 603,602.06, and by Anshan Finance Bureau in the amount of RMB 10,247.94.

During the second instance, the parties did not submit new evidence. This Court confirms the facts found in the first instance.

This Court holds that the disputed issues in this case are: 1. How should the validity of the Share Transfer Contract No. 2012-jr003 in question be determined; 2. How should the method of rescission of the Share Transfer Contract No. 2012-jr003 in question be determined; 3. Whether Anshan Finance Bureau should compensate Biaobang Company for transaction costs, deposit interest loss, and loss of expected profit.

(1) The Share Transfer Contract No. 2012-jr003 in question should be determined as a contract that was formed but not yet effective.

Contract Law of the People's Republic of China Article 44 provides that a contract lawfully formed shall become effective upon its formation. Where laws or administrative regulations require approval, registration, or other formalities to be completed for a contract to become effective, such provisions shall govern. Article 2 of the Circular on Strengthening the Administration of Property Rights Transactions of State-Owned Enterprises, issued by the General Office of the State Council as Guo Ban Fa Dian (1994) No. 12, provides that the transfer of property rights of state-owned enterprises under local administration shall be subject to the approval of the people's government at or above the prefecture level; where there is central investment, the consent of the relevant department of the State Council shall be obtained in advance, and the property rights income belonging to the central investment portion shall be turned over to the central government. The transfer of property rights of state-owned enterprises under central administration shall be submitted by the relevant department of the State Council to the State Council for approval. The transfer of property rights of all super-large and large state-owned enterprises (including those under local administration) shall be submitted to the State Council for approval. Article 7 of the Measures for the Administration of the Transfer of State-Owned Assets of Financial Enterprises of the Ministry of Finance provides that the transfer of state-owned assets of financial enterprises shall be supervised and managed by the financial departments under the principle of unified policies and hierarchical management. Where a financial department transfers state-owned assets of a financial enterprise, it shall submit to the people's government at the same level for approval. Where a government-authorized investment entity transfers state-owned assets of a financial enterprise, it shall submit to the financial department at the same level for approval. Where matters involving government social public administration and financial industry supervision and management arise in the process of transferring state-owned assets of financial enterprises, they shall be submitted to the relevant government department for approval in accordance with state regulations. Article 28 of the Commercial Banking Law of the People's Republic of China provides that any unit or individual that purchases more than five percent of the total shares of a commercial bank shall obtain prior approval from the banking regulatory authority of the State Council. The subject matter of the Share Transfer Contract in this case is the 9.9986% equity, i.e., 225 million shares, of Anshan Bank held by Anshan Finance Bureau, which constitutes state-owned assets of a financial enterprise, and the total shares transferred have exceeded 5% of the total shares of Anshan Bank. Pursuant to the above provisions, the contract shall take legal effect only after approval by the government and the financial industry supervision and management department having the approval authority. Accordingly, although the Share Transfer Contract in this case has been formed, it has not been approved by the competent authority and shall be determined to be not yet effective. Biaobang Company's assertion that the contract has been approved by the Anshan Municipal People's Government is based on the Anshan State-Owned Bank Equity Transfer Prospectus, but that prospectus is merely an approval by the Anshan Municipal People's Government for the listing and transfer of the equity in question, and is not an approval of the Share Transfer Contract. Therefore, Biaobang Company's ground of appeal that the contract has become effective does not comply with legal provisions and cannot be sustained.

(2) Regarding how to determine the method of rescission of the Share Transfer Contract.

1. The Share Transfer Contract shall be determined to have been rescinded by mutual agreement on October 11, 2013. Article 93 of the Contract Law provides that the parties may rescind a contract by mutual agreement. The parties may agree on the conditions for a party to rescind the contract. When the conditions for rescission are satisfied, the party entitled to rescind may rescind the contract. In this case, Anshan Finance Bureau, by letter An Cai Zhai [2013] No. 137, issued to Shenyang Equity Exchange on June 6, 2013, a letter titled "Letter on Terminating the Transfer of State-Owned Equity in Anshan Bank," citing significant appreciation of state-owned assets. Based on this letter, Shenyang Equity Exchange issued on June 14, 2013 a notice to Biaobang Company, Hongyun Group, CITIC Honghe Mining Co., Ltd., and Liaoning Rongxin Asset Management Co., Ltd., terminating the transfer of state-owned equity in Anshan Bank. On October 11, 2013, Hongyun Group, on behalf of the four listed companies, issued to Anshan Finance Bureau a "Letter on Requesting the Return of Transaction Deposit." Although this letter did not explicitly agree to rescind the contract, it did not advocate for continued performance of the contract; instead, it made demands regarding how to handle the post-rescission matters, namely requesting the return of the deposit and payment of transaction fees. This reply letter should be deemed as an indication of agreement to rescind the contract. Accordingly, the original judgment's finding that the parties reached a mutual agreement to rescind the contract on October 11, 2013 is lawful and well-founded.

2. The grounds of appeal by Anshan Finance Bureau and Biaobang Company that the contract was unilaterally rescinded are both untenable. Article 96 of the Contract Law provides for the exercise of the right to rescind a contract. Only when the conditions for rescission agreed upon in the contract as provided in Article 93(2) of the Contract Law are satisfied, or when the circumstances set forth in Article 94(1) through (5) exist, does a party have the right to unilaterally rescind the contract, and the time of rescission is the time when the notice of rescission reaches the other party. On the one hand, although the Anshan State-owned Assets Supervision and Administration Commission issued a "Letter on Terminating the Transfer of State-Owned Equity in Anshan Bank" on March 27, 2013, to which Biaobang Company and others responded with a letter of objection on April 11, 2013, the Anshan State-owned Assets Supervision and Administration Commission is not a party to the contract. Anshan Finance Bureau has no evidence that the intent expressed by the Anshan State-owned Assets Supervision and Administration Commission could be regarded as the intent of Anshan Finance Bureau itself. Therefore, the letter from the Anshan State-owned Assets Supervision and Administration Commission terminating the transaction cannot produce the legal effect of rescinding the contract. Anshan Finance Bureau's ground of appeal that the contract was rescinded by the letter from the Anshan State-owned Assets Supervision and Administration Commission terminating the transfer is legally unfounded and cannot be sustained. On the other hand, based on the foregoing analysis, with respect to Anshan Finance Bureau's letter terminating the transaction sent to Shenyang Equity Exchange, Biaobang Company and others had already sent a letter indicating agreement, and the parties reached an agreement to rescind the contract. Accordingly, the contract should be determined to have been rescinded by mutual agreement on October 11, 2013. Biaobang Company's ground of appeal that the contract was unilaterally rescinded by Anshan Finance Bureau on June 14, 2013 is inconsistent with the facts and cannot be sustained.

(3) Regarding whether Anshan Finance Bureau should compensate Biaobang Company for transaction fees, deposit interest, and loss of expected profits.

Article 4 of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China provides that civil activities shall adhere to the principles of voluntariness, fairness, equal value and compensation, and good faith. Article 42 of the Contract Law provides that if a party, during the process of entering into a contract, falls under any of the following circumstances, causing loss to the other party, it shall be liable for damages: (1) negotiating in bad faith under the pretext of concluding a contract; (2) intentionally concealing important facts related to the conclusion of the contract or providing false information; (3) engaging in other acts contrary to the principle of good faith. The above legal provisions establish the liability for fault in contracting, i.e., if during the process of contract negotiation, a party violates the principle of good faith and fails to perform its relevant pre-contractual obligations, it shall bear liability for damages for the losses suffered by the other party as a result. Based on legal provisions and the facts of this case, the nature of the liability to be borne by Anshan Finance Bureau after the rescission of the contract, the scope of compensation, and the specific amounts are analyzed as follows:

1. Anshan Finance Bureau committed fault in contracting by failing to submit the contract for approval.

First, Anshan Finance Bureau's failure to perform its application for approval obligation violated the contract. Article 8 of the Contract Law provides that a contract lawfully formed is legally binding on the parties. The parties shall perform their obligations in accordance with the agreement and shall not alter or rescind the contract without authorization. A lawfully formed contract is protected by law. Article 8 of the Supreme People's Court's Interpretation (II) on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the Contract Law provides that after a contract that requires approval or registration in accordance with laws or administrative regulations to become effective is formed, if the party obligated to apply for approval or registration fails to apply for approval or registration in accordance with the law or the contract, such failure constitutes "other acts contrary to the principle of good faith" under Article 42(3) of the Contract Law. The people's court may, based on the specific circumstances of the case and the request of the other party, order the other party to handle the relevant procedures on its own; the party in breach shall bear liability for damages for the expenses incurred and the actual losses suffered by the other party as a result. According to the above legal provisions and judicial interpretation, if a contract has been formed, although the relevant provisions on equity transfer in the contract need approval from the competent authority to take effect, the provisions on the obligation to apply for approval are legally binding on the parties from the time the contract is formed. The parties shall perform the obligation to apply for approval in accordance with the contract and actively facilitate the contract's effectiveness. In this case, Article 7.1 of the Share Transfer Contract provides that this transfer shall, in accordance with the law, be submitted to the competent authority for approval. Party A and Party B shall perform or assist in performing the obligation to submit to the approval authority. They shall use best efforts to cooperate in dealing with any reasonable requirements or inquiries raised by the approval authority to obtain approval of this contract and the equity transaction hereunder. Article 11.2 provides that Biaobang Company, as Party B, guarantees that all certifications and materials submitted to Party A and Shenyang Equity Exchange are true, accurate, and complete. Although the above provisions do not clearly specify which party bears the obligation to apply for approval or the obligation to assist in applying for approval, based on the agreement, Biaobang Company's primary obligation is to provide relevant certifications and materials, i.e., to assist in applying for approval. Accordingly, it should be determined that the obligation to apply for approval under the contract is borne by Anshan Finance Bureau. However, Anshan Finance Bureau violated the contract by failing to perform the obligation to apply for approval and also failing to supplement and submit relevant materials as required by the competent authority. Pursuant to the above judicial interpretation, its conduct constitutes "other acts contrary to the principle of good faith" under Article 42(3) of the Contract Law, and it should be determined that Anshan Finance Bureau committed fault in contracting. Anshan Bank is not a party to the Share Transfer Contract. Anshan Finance Bureau's ground of appeal that the obligation to apply for approval is borne by Anshan Bank has no contractual basis and is not supported.

Second, Anshan Finance Bureau's defense for not performing the obligation to apply for approval is untenable. On the one hand, Anshan Finance Bureau's claim that Biaobang Company and the other three enterprises had an affiliated relationship resulting in their lack of qualification to acquire the equity in question lacks sufficient evidence. According to the facts found, the Anshan State-owned Assets Supervision and Administration Commission, on March 25, 2013, issued An Guo Zi Han [2013] No. 13, a "Letter on Terminating the Acceptance of State-Owned Equity in Anshan Bank," terminating the equity transfer on the grounds of related transactions among Biaobang Company and the other three enterprises. However, after Biaobang Company and others raised objections, the Anshan State-owned Assets Supervision and Administration Commission, on May 2, 2013, issued another letter to conduct an audit of the materials submitted by Biaobang Company and the other three enterprises, and to submit the audit results to the regulatory authorities for review. Since the audit report was prepared before the time Anshan Finance Bureau terminated the equity transfer, and the audit conclusion did not clearly negate the qualification of Biaobang Company and others to acquire the equity, Anshan Finance Bureau's ground of appeal that Biaobang Company lacked qualification to acquire the equity due to affiliated relationships, lack of sufficient evidence, is untenable. On the other hand, Anshan Finance Bureau's refusal to submit the approval materials has no legal basis. Having entered into the contract with Biaobang Company, Anshan Finance Bureau should be deemed to have recognized Biaobang Company's qualification as a contracting party. Whether the Share Transfer Contract is approved should be decided by the government and the financial industry regulatory authorities. As a party to the contract, Anshan Finance Bureau does not have the approval authority and cannot, based on its own judgment, violate the contract and exempt itself from the obligation to submit for approval. Anshan Finance Bureau's ground of appeal that the contract did not require submission for approval because Biaobang Company lacked qualification has no factual or legal basis and cannot be sustained.

In summary, Anshan Finance Bureau, without justifiable reason, failed to perform its obligation to apply for approval under the contract. Its conduct constitutes "other acts contrary to the principle of good faith" under Article 42 of the Contract Law, and it should be determined to have committed fault in contracting.

2. Anshan Finance Bureau shall compensate Biaobang Company for its direct losses.

Based on the above analysis, Anshan Finance Bureau violated the principle of good faith and committed fault in contracting. The transaction fees and deposit interest paid by Biaobang Company during the contract negotiation process constitute direct losses of Biaobang Company, for which Anshan Finance Bureau shall bear liability for compensation. The specific analysis is as follows: First, regarding the transaction fees and interest. According to the facts found, Biaobang Company paid the transaction fees to Shenyang Equity Exchange on March 30, 2012, and the deposit returned by Anshan Finance Bureau also deducted the transaction fees. These fees represent a reduction in Biaobang Company's actual property during the contract formation process, and both the fees and the corresponding interest shall be compensated by Anshan Finance Bureau. Biaobang Company had guaranteed to Shenyang Equity Exchange that the transaction fees would not be refunded regardless of whether the transaction was successful. Therefore, in the case of an unsuccessful transaction, the transaction fees have already constituted a loss to Biaobang Company, caused by Anshan Finance Bureau's dishonest conduct. Therefore, Anshan Finance Bureau's ground of appeal that it should not be liable for compensation is untenable. Second, regarding the deposit interest. Although Anshan Finance Bureau has returned the deposit paid by Biaobang Company, Biaobang Company, as a commercial entity, incurred financial costs due to the payment of the deposit, regardless of whether it used its own funds. Therefore, the corresponding interest on the deposit paid by Biaobang Company constitutes a direct loss and shall be compensated by Anshan Finance Bureau. Finally, regarding the standard for calculating interest. The original judgment's use of the People's Bank of China's loan interest rate for the same period as the standard for calculating interest on the transaction fees and deposit interest complies with the usual calculation standard and is not improper. Anshan Finance Bureau's claim that the standard should be the deposit interest rate for the same period has no legal basis and is not supported. Anshan Finance Bureau's ground of appeal that non-payment of interest is an industry practice lacks evidence and shall not be accepted.

3. Anshan Finance Bureau shall appropriately compensate Biaobang Company for the loss of expected profits claimed.

(1) The loss of a party's objective and reasonable transaction opportunity should fall within the scope of compensation for liability for fault in contracting. The system of liability for fault in contracting is a specific safeguard for implementing the basic civil law principle of good faith. By requiring the party at fault in contracting to bear liability for damages, it fills the reliance interest loss of the good faith counterparty, thereby urging all types of civil subjects to act with integrity and keep their promises. Typically, compensating the good faith counterparty for direct losses such as expenses incurred during contract negotiation under liability for fault in contracting can restore the counterparty's interests. However, if the good faith counterparty indeed suffers indirect losses, such as loss of transaction opportunities, due to the conduct of the party at fault in contracting, the party at fault should also provide appropriate compensation. On the one hand, there is no legal basis for exempting the party at fault in contracting from liability for compensating the counterparty's indirect losses. The "losses" referred to in Article 42 of the Contract Law are not limited to direct losses. Article 8 of the Supreme People's Court's Interpretation (II) on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the Contract Law provides that when a party obligated to apply for approval fails to do so in a contract that takes effect only upon approval, if the contract can still be submitted for approval and the counterparty chooses to handle the approval procedures on its own, the counterparty may handle the procedures itself, and the party at fault in contracting shall compensate the counterparty for its relevant actual losses. None of the above provisions exclude the liability of the party at fault in contracting for compensating the counterparty's indirect losses such as loss of transaction opportunities. On the other hand, requiring the party at fault in contracting to bear liability for compensating the counterparty's objective and reasonable indirect losses is also an inherent requirement for implementing the principle of good faith and protecting the interests of the non-breaching party. Although the inherent uncertainty of transaction opportunities affects the determination of the amount of corresponding damages, which should be determined based on the specific circumstances of the case, this should not serve as a basis to completely exempt the party at fault in contracting from liability for indirect losses.

(2) Regarding whether Anshan Finance Bureau should be liable for compensating Biaobang Company's other losses.

First, Anshan Finance Bureau's fault in maliciously preventing the contract from taking effect is clear. As a government department, in the process of state-owned property rights transactions, Anshan Finance Bureau should not only practice the value of good faith and keep its promises, but also follow the principle of government integrity to earn public trust and lead the whole society in building an honest and trustworthy market order. However, in this case, when it could have submitted the contract to the competent authority for approval, it refused to submit the corresponding materials as required by the banking regulatory authority, resulting in the regulatory authority not accepting the relevant administrative licensing matter, thereby preventing the contract from taking effect. Moreover, it sold the equity in question at a higher price within a very short period. Anshan Finance Bureau maliciously prevented the contract from taking effect, and its conduct clearly violated the principle of good faith, with obvious fault.

Second, Biaobang Company suffered an objective and reasonable loss of transaction opportunity. The loss of expected profits claimed by Biaobang Company is essentially the loss of the opportunity to acquire the equity in question. An opportunity refers to a state where some conditions for the formation of a specific benefit or the avoidance of a specific harm are already in place, but whether it can ultimately be realized remains uncertain. A loss of opportunity is the reduction or loss of the possibility for a party to obtain a specific benefit or avoid a specific harm. Generally, at the stage of contract negotiation, whether a contract can be concluded and whether the transaction opportunity brought about by the contract can ultimately be realized are unknown, so the transaction opportunity is not yet possible at that time. However, if the parties have reached consensus and signed a contract, before the conditions for the contract's effectiveness are satisfied, the degree of mutual trust between the parties has reached a higher level, and the opportunity to obtain specific benefits based on reliance on the other party's honest performance of relevant obligations also has considerable possibility. At this point, if one party fails to act honestly in performing the obligation to apply for approval, it should foresee that the other party will suffer losses as a result. In this case, after the Share Transfer Contract was concluded, although it required approval from the competent authority to become effective, the parties had reached consensus on Biaobang Company's purchase of Anshan Bank equity. In the absence of evidence that the contract could not obtain approval from the competent authority, Biaobang Company had reasonable grounds to trust that Anshan Finance Bureau would keep its promise and timely and properly perform the approval procedures, thereby confirming the effectiveness of the contract and then actually acquiring the equity in question and obtaining related benefits through the performance of the contract. Therefore, the possibility for Biaobang Company to obtain the equity in question realistically existed. However, because Anshan Finance Bureau refused to submit the contract for approval and subsequently sold the equity at a higher price, its dishonest conduct directly caused the complete loss of the possibility for Biaobang Company to obtain the equity, thereby entirely eliminating the reality of Biaobang Company obtaining related benefits. In summary, Biaobang Company suffered an objective and realistic loss of transaction opportunity due to Anshan Finance Bureau's dishonest conduct.

Finally, Anshan Finance Bureau's liability for compensating Biaobang Company's loss of transaction opportunity is necessary to uphold fairness, justice, and the order of market transactions. On the one hand, requiring Anshan Finance Bureau to compensate for Biaobang Company's loss of transaction opportunity is consistent with the principle of fairness. The benefit Anshan Finance Bureau obtained from selling the equity at a price difference came at the cost of Biaobang Company losing the opportunity to purchase the equity. If, under the circumstances where Anshan Finance Bureau gained benefits from its wrongful conduct, Biaobang Company's loss of transaction opportunity is not compensated, the interests of the two parties would be severely imbalanced, which is not in line with the principle of fairness. On the other hand, requiring Anshan Finance Bureau to bear appropriate compensation for Biaobang Company's indirect losses, in addition to compensating its direct losses, so that it pays a corresponding price for its dishonest conduct, will help urge all types of civil subjects to act with integrity, abide by good faith, and help maintain an honest and trustworthy market transaction order.

(3) Determination of the amount of loss from lost transaction opportunity of Biaobang Company. Based on the facts of this case, the amount of loss from lost transaction opportunity suffered by Biaobang Company due to the contract not taking effect shall be determined by comprehensively considering the following factors: First, the benefit gained by Anshan Finance Bureau. As stated above, Anshan Finance Bureau, in violation of the principle of good faith, sold the involved equity to another party at the price of RMB 2.5 per share, and the price difference of RMB 0.5 per share it obtained was derived from its dishonest conduct. The amount of Biaobang Company's loss from losing the opportunity to transact for the involved equity may be determined by reference to this. Second, the transaction costs incurred by Biaobang Company. Since the involved contract did not take effect and has been rescinded, Biaobang Company did not actually pay the consideration nor actually acquire the involved equity. Its claim that the compensation should be based on the full amount of the price difference from Anshan Finance Bureau's resale of the equity is inconsistent with the circumstances of this case and should not be sustained. In this case, even if Biaobang Company had actually acquired the involved equity, because the contract between the parties contained a restriction on the time period for further transfer of the equity, the value of the involved equity after the expiry of the agreed period — whether it would rise or fall — remained uncertain. In addition, although Biaobang Company lost the transaction opportunity to purchase the involved equity, this did not prevent it from subsequently investing its funds in other projects to obtain returns. In summary, for Biaobang Company's loss from the lost transaction opportunity, this Court determines it in its discretion at 10% of the price difference from Anshan Finance Bureau's resale of the involved equity, calculated as follows: (the resale price of the involved equity of RMB 2.5 per share minus the contract price for transfer of the involved equity of RMB 2 per share) multiplied by 225 million shares multiplied by 10%, i.e., RMB 11.25 million. This loss shall be compensated by Anshan Finance Bureau.

(IV) Biaobang Company's lawsuit was not filed beyond the statute of limitations.

Article 135 of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the PRC provides that the statute of limitations for requesting protection of civil rights from a people's court is two years, unless otherwise provided by law. Article 137 provides that the statute of limitations shall be calculated from the time when the person knows or should have known that his rights have been infringed. As stated above, the involved contract was rescinded on October 11, 2013, and Biaobang Company simultaneously clearly requested the return of the deposit and transaction fees. At that time, Biaobang Company knew that its interests had been harmed, so the statute of limitations for claiming protection of its rights should be calculated from October 11, 2013. On January 16, 2014, Biaobang Company filed a lawsuit against Anshan Finance Bureau to assert its rights, causing an interruption of the statute of limitations, which should be recalculated from that date. Biaobang Company filed the present lawsuit on September 1, 2015, which does not exceed the two-year statute of limitations period. Anshan Finance Bureau's appellate argument that Biaobang Company's lawsuit exceeded the statute of limitations lacks factual basis and is not sustained.

In summary, the facts found in the original judgment are clear, but the handling of the issue of compensation for Biaobang Company's lost profits is improper and should be corrected. Pursuant to Article 42 of the Contract Law of the PRC and subparagraph (2) of Article 170 of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC, the judgment is as follows:

1. Affirm items 1, 2, and 3 of the civil judgment (2015) Liao Min Er Chu Zi No. 00060 of the Liaoning High People's Court;

2. Reverse item 4 of the civil judgment (2015) Liao Min Er Chu Zi No. 00060 of the Liaoning High People's Court;

3. Anshan Finance Bureau shall, within fifteen days after this judgment takes effect, compensate Shenzhen Biaobang Investment Development Co., Ltd. for losses in the amount of RMB 11.25 million;

4. Dismiss the other claims of Shenzhen Biaobang Investment Development Co., Ltd.

If the monetary payment obligation is not fulfilled within the period specified in this judgment, interest on the debt during the period of delayed performance shall be doubled in accordance with Article 253 of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC.
